examples.solution_text:
(a) Multiply each term inside by $4$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}4(t+6)\\&=4(t)+4(6)\\&=4t+24\end{aligned}$
(b) Keep the subtraction sign.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}5(2h-3)\\&=5(2h)-5(3)\\&=10h-15\end{aligned}$

(a) Treat the second term as $-5$. A negative times a negative is positive.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-3(2p-5)\\&=(-3)(2p)+(-3)(-5)\\&=-6p+15\end{aligned}$
(b) The minus in front means multiply by $-1$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-(4q+7)\\&=(-1)(4q)+(-1)(7)\\&=-4q-7\end{aligned}$

Multiply both terms by $3x$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3x(2x-y)\\&=3x(2x)-3x(y)\\&=6x^2-3xy\end{aligned}$
The two terms are unlike, so they cannot be collected.

(a) Multiply all three terms by $2$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2(a-3b+4)\\&=2(a)-2(3b)+2(4)\\&=2a-6b+8\end{aligned}$
(b) Expand each bracket, including the negative multiplier on the second bracket.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3(2z+1)-2(z-4)\\&=6z+3-2z+8\\&=4z+11\end{aligned}$

(a) Multiply each term by $3xy$. Keep every variable factor.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3xy(2x-4y)\\&=3xy(2x)-3xy(4y)\\&=6x^2y-12xy^2\end{aligned}$
(b) Multiply all three terms by $2a$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2a(3a+4b+5)\\&=2a(3a)+2a(4b)+2a(5)\\&=6a^2+8ab+10a\end{aligned}$
